extraction.segment_function: The block defines the distinction between work and labor through the concepts of homo faber, the human artifice, durability, and objectivity, contrasting the stability of man-made things with the cyclical nature of biological consumption.

definitions.definition: The maker who literally works upon materials and fabricates the things that constitute the human artifice.
The laborer who labors and mixes with biological processes.

distinctions.distinction: Work is the activity of hands by homo faber that makes and works upon things to create a durable human artifice, whereas labor is the activity of animal laborans that mixes with biological processes.
Destruction is inherent in consumption, whereas wear is incidental to use, as use objects possess an independence and durability that allows them to survive even when unused.

must_not_be_lost: The distinction between homo faber and animal laborans.
The role of durability and objectivity in stabilizing human life and identity.
